problem.claim: The paper addresses computationally tractable relaxations of variational inequalities, whose goal is to find a distribution satisfying the VI constraint in expectation.

contributions.claim: Introduces expected variational inequalities (EVIs), a distributional relaxation requiring the VI constraint to hold in expectation.
Analyzes EVIs using techniques adapted from game theory and reports polynomial-time solvability under general nonmonotone operators.
Relates EVIs to correlated equilibria and uses the framework to capture or generalize results from smooth games and games with coupled constraints or nonconcave utilities.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present EVIs as a natural expectation-based relaxation of VIs with applicability extending beyond games.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that EVIs can be solved in polynomial time under general, nonmonotone operators, unlike VIs.
The authors report that EVIs capture correlated equilibria while reaching beyond game settings.
The authors report that their framework captures and generalizes disparate prior results involving smooth games, coupled constraints, and nonconcave utilities.

narrative_sequence.summary: VIs are broadly applicable, but their expressivity is associated with computational intractability.
The paper introduces EVIs, requiring a distribution to satisfy the VI constraint in expectation.
Game-theoretic techniques are adapted to report polynomial-time solvability for EVIs with general nonmonotone operators.
The framework is connected to correlated equilibria and extended to settings beyond games, including several game variants.

source_observation.claim: The abstract defines a relaxation, states a tractability contrast with the original problem, and then identifies conceptual coverage and generalizations.

lessons.interpretation: A compact research narrative can align a formal relaxation with both a computational payoff and a broader unifying scope.
lessons.application: When proposing a relaxation, explicitly state its constraint, the resulting computational claim, and which known concepts or cases it subsumes.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when no formal relaxation, computational comparison, or concrete coverage claims are available.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the algorithm, polynomial runtime dependence, or precise assumptions beyond general nonmonotone operators.
It does not detail how EVIs extend beyond games or which exact prior results are generalized.
No empirical setup, benchmarks, or independently verifiable proof details are provided.
